module AST.Semantics.Type

-- | Enumeration of all possible types in the language.
data Type
TyInt :: Type
TyBool :: Type
TyVoid :: Type
TyList :: Type -> Type
TyFunc :: [Type] -> Type -> Type
TyStruct :: Text -> Type
TyAuto :: Type

-- | Definition of a structure (Name + Field Map).
data StructDef
StructDef :: Text -> Map Text Type -> StructDef
[structName] :: StructDef -> Text
[structFields] :: StructDef -> Map Text Type

-- | Verification Environment.
data CheckEnv
CheckEnv :: Map Text Type -> Map Text StructDef -> CheckEnv
[envVars] :: CheckEnv -> Map Text Type
[envStructs] :: CheckEnv -> Map Text StructDef

-- | Initial empty environment.
emptyEnv :: CheckEnv

-- | Parses a raw type string (from Parser) into a Semantic Type.
parseType :: Text -> Type

-- | Helper to convert a Semantic Type back to a readable String.
typeToString :: Type -> String

-- | Checks if two types are semantically compatible. Replaces usage of
--   (==) with explicit pattern matching.
areTypesCompatible :: Type -> Type -> Bool
instance GHC.Classes.Eq AST.Semantics.Type.Type
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show AST.Semantics.Type.CheckEnv
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show AST.Semantics.Type.StructDef
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show AST.Semantics.Type.Type


-- | This module provides tools to transform technical Megaparsec errors
--   into human-readable, colored error messages. It helps standardize
--   error reporting across the entire application (Parsing, Semantics,
--   Imports).
module Common.Error

-- | Main entry point to format a Megaparsec error bundle.
--   
--   @args - bundle: The full error bundle returned by <tt>parse</tt>.
--   
--   @details Extracts the first error, calculates position, and formats
--   the message. Refactored to meet coding style (short function, short
--   lines).
formatParseError :: ParseErrorBundle Text Void -> String

-- | Formats a generic error message with a colored tag.
--   
--   @args - tag: The error category (e.g., "Semantic Error", "Import
--   Error"). - msg: The error description.
--   
--   @return A formatted string with the tag in red ANSI color.
formatError :: String -> String -> String

-- | Format <a>FancyError</a> messages (generated by <a>fail</a>).
--   
--   @details Iterates over the set of fancy errors and extracts the text
--   message if it exists (ErrorFail).
formatFancyError :: Set (ErrorFancy Void) -> String

-- | Extracts the "expected" tokens from a ParseError.
--   
--   @args - err: The Megaparsec error object.
--   
--   @return A clean string listing expected tokens or "custom error".
getExpected :: ParseError Text Void -> String

-- | Extracts the "unexpected" token from a ParseError.
--   
--   @args - err: The Megaparsec error object.
--   
--   @return A string describing what was found instead (e.g., "end of
--   input", ""foo"").
getUnexpected :: ParseError Text Void -> String

module Common.Type.Integer
data IntValue
I8 :: Int8 -> IntValue
UI8 :: Word8 -> IntValue
I16 :: Int16 -> IntValue
UI16 :: Word16 -> IntValue
I32 :: Int32 -> IntValue
UI32 :: Word32 -> IntValue
I64 :: Int64 -> IntValue
UI64 :: Word64 -> IntValue
IChar :: Int8 -> IntValue
UIChar :: Word8 -> IntValue

-- | Converts an IntValue to a standard Haskell Int.
--   
--   @args - v: The IntValue to convert.
--   
--   @details This function handles all IntValue constructors, converting
--   them to the system's native <a>Int</a> type. Note that converting
--   large 64-bit values on a 32-bit system might cause overflow, though
--   this is rare in modern environments.
--   
--   @return The integer value as an <a>Int</a>.
intValueToInt :: IntValue -> Int

-- | Converts an arbitrary Integer to the smallest suitable IntValue.
--   
--   @args - n: The Integer to compress.
--   
--   @details Similar to <a>fromInt64</a> but works on arbitrary precision
--   <a>Integer</a>s. It attempts to fit the value into I8<i>UI8, then
--   I16</i>UI16, etc. If the value exceeds the signed 64-bit range but
--   fits in unsigned 64-bit, it uses UI64.
--   
--   @return The optimized <a>IntValue</a>.
fitInteger :: Integer -> IntValue

-- | Converts an IntValue to a standard Haskell Int64.
--   
--   @args - v: The IntValue to convert.
--   
--   @details Provides a safe conversion to <a>Int64</a> for all underlying
--   types. Unsigned 64-bit values are treated as signed (wrapping) if they
--   exceed 'maxBound :: Int64'.
--   
--   @return The integer value as an <a>Int64</a>.
toInt64 :: IntValue -> Int64

-- | Converts an Int64 to the smallest suitable IntValue representation.
--   
--   @args - n: The Int64 value to compress.
--   
--   @details This function checks the bounds of the integer to determine
--   the most compact storage format (I8, UI8, I16, etc.). It prioritizes
--   signed representation for small positive numbers but will use unsigned
--   types if it saves space (e.g., 200 fits in UI8 but requires I16).
--   
--   @return An <a>IntValue</a> wrapping the value in the smallest possible
--   container.
fromInt64 :: Int64 -> IntValue
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Common.Type.Integer.IntValue
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Common.Type.Integer.IntValue
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Common.Type.Integer.IntValue

module AST.Ast

-- | Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definition for the GLADOS language.
--   
--   @details The AST represents the hierarchical structure of the parsed
--   source code. Each constructor corresponds to a specific syntactic
--   construct in the language, such as literals, definitions, control
--   flow, and function calls.
data Ast

-- | Represents an integer literal. @param IntValue The value of the
--   integer.
AInteger :: IntValue -> Ast

-- | Represents a boolean literal. @param Bool True or False.
ABool :: Bool -> Ast

-- | Represents a symbol (identifier). Used for variable names, function
--   names, or reference lookups. @param Text The name of the symbol.
ASymbol :: Text -> Ast

-- | Represents a Void or Null value (no return value).
AVoid :: Ast

-- | Represents a generic list of AST nodes. Can be used for list literals
--   or sequence of expressions. @param [Ast] The elements of the list.
AList :: [Ast] -> Ast

-- | Represents a named function definition. <tt>param Text The name of the
--   function. </tt>param [(Text, Text)] The list of arguments (Name,
--   Type). <tt>param Text The return type of the function. </tt>param Ast
--   The body of the function.
ADefineFunc :: Text -> [(Text, Text)] -> Text -> Ast -> Ast

-- | Represents an anonymous function (Lambda). <tt>param [Text] The list
--   of parameter names. </tt>param Ast The body of the lambda.
ADefineLambda :: [Text] -> Ast -> Ast

-- | Represents a structure type definition. <tt>param Text The name of the
--   structure. </tt>param [(Text, Text)] The list of fields (Name, Type).
ADefineStruct :: Text -> [(Text, Text)] -> Ast

-- | Represents a variable definition or assignment. <tt>param Text The
--   name of the variable. </tt>param Text The type of the variable. @param
--   Ast The value assigned to the variable.
ASetVar :: Text -> Text -> Ast -> Ast

-- | Represents a structure definition statement wrapper. @param
--   ADefineStruct The structure definition node.
ASetStruct :: Text -> [(Text, Ast)] -> Ast

-- | Represents a function call (Application). <tt>param Ast The callee
--   (function expression or symbol). </tt>param [Ast] The list of
--   arguments passed to the function.
ACall :: Ast -> [Ast] -> Ast

-- | Represents a field access (e.g., player.x). <tt>param Ast The
--   object/structure being accessed. </tt>param Text The name of the
--   field.
AAccessStruct :: Ast -> Text -> Ast

-- | Represents an import statement. @param Text The name of the module or
--   file to import.
AImport :: Text -> Ast

-- | Represents a conditional control flow (If-Then-Else). <tt>param Ast
--   The condition expression. </tt>param Ast The <a>Then</a> branch.
--   @param Ast The <a>Else</a> branch.
AIf :: Ast -> Ast -> Ast -> Ast

-- | Represents a While loop. <tt>param Ast The loop condition. </tt>param
--   Ast The loop body.
AWhile :: Ast -> Ast -> Ast

-- | Represents a For loop. <tt>param Ast The initialization step.
--   </tt>param Ast The loop condition. <tt>param Ast The update/increment
--   step. </tt>param Ast The loop body.
AFor :: Ast -> Ast -> Ast -> Ast -> Ast

-- | Represents an explicit return statement. @param Ast The expression to
--   return.
AReturn :: Ast -> Ast

-- | Represents an expression used as a statement. This wrapper is used
--   when an expression is executed for its side effects (e.g., a function
--   call or assignment) rather than its return value. Usually corresponds
--   to an expression followed by a semicolon. @param Ast The wrapped
--   expression.
AExprStmt :: Ast -> Ast

-- | Represents a scoped block of code (enclosed in braces `{}`). Used to
--   group multiple statements into a single logical unit, typically for
--   function bodies, loop bodies, or conditional branches. @param [Ast]
--   The list of statements contained in the block.
ABlock :: [Ast] -> Ast

-- | Represents a <a>break</a> statement. Used to immediately terminate the
--   nearest enclosing loop (for, while). Control flow continues at the
--   next statement following the loop.
ABreak :: Ast

-- | Represents a source code position wrapper. Used for precise error
--   reporting (line, column). This node wraps another AST node without
--   changing its semantics. <tt>param Int The line number. </tt>param Int
--   The column number. @param Ast The wrapped AST node.
APos :: Int -> Int -> Ast -> Ast
showAst :: Ast -> String
printAst :: Ast -> IO ()

-- | Recursively removes all position wrappers (APos) from the AST.
--   
--   This is useful for: Pretty printing (to avoid cluttering the output
--   with position data). Testing (to compare AST structure without
--   worrying about line numbers).
--   
--   <tt>param Ast The AST potentially containing APos nodes. </tt>return
--   Ast The cleaned AST with purely structural nodes.
cleanAst :: Ast -> Ast
instance GHC.Classes.Eq AST.Ast.Ast
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show AST.Ast.Ast

module AST.Semantics.CheckCall

-- | Main entry point for checking calls and operators.
--   
--   Dispatches the call to the appropriate handler. It first checks if the
--   function is a built-in operator (Math, Logic, Special). If not, it
--   attempts to resolve it as a user-defined function.
--   
--   <tt>param CheckExprFn The callback to verify arguments. </tt>param
--   CheckEnv The current semantic environment. <tt>param Ast The function
--   node (usually ASymbol). </tt>param [Ast] The list of arguments.
--   @return Either String Type The return type of the call or an error
--   message.
checkCall :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> Ast -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates equality checks (==).
--   
--   Unlike other binary ops, equality allows any type as long as both
--   operands have compatible types (e.g. int==int, bool==bool).
checkEqualityOp :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates 'typeof(arg)'.
--   
--   Introspection function that returns the type of the argument as a
--   string. It accepts any valid expression type.
--   
--   <tt>param arg: Any expression. </tt>return: String (TyList TyInt)
--   representing the type name (e.g., "int", "bool").
checkTypeof :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates 'ffread(path)'.
--   
--   High-level File Read: Reads the entire content of a file.
--   
--   <tt>param path: String (TyList TyInt) representing the file path.
--   </tt>return: [String] (TyList (TyList TyInt)), where each element is a
--   line.
checkFFRead :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates 'ffwrite(path, content)'.
--   
--   High-level File Write: Writes a list of strings to a file.
--   
--   <tt>param path: String (TyList TyInt) representing the file path.
--   </tt>param content: [String] (TyList (TyList TyInt)) the lines to
--   write. @return: Bool (TyBool) indicating success or failure.
checkFFWrite :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates 'open(path, mode)'.
--   
--   Low-level Open: Opens a file and returns a file descriptor.
--   
--   <tt>param path: String (TyList TyInt) representing the file path.
--   </tt>param mode: Int (TyInt) representing the access mode (e.g., 0 for
--   read, 1 for write). @return: Int (TyInt) the file descriptor (FD).
checkOpen :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates 'close(fd)'.
--   
--   Low-level Close: Closes an open file descriptor.
--   
--   <tt>param fd: Int (TyInt) the file descriptor to close. </tt>return:
--   Int (TyInt) usually 0 for success.
checkClose :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates 'read(fd, size)'.
--   
--   Low-level Read: Reads a specific number of bytes/characters from a
--   file descriptor.
--   
--   <tt>param fd: Int (TyInt) the file descriptor to read from. </tt>param
--   size: Int (TyInt) the number of characters to read. @return: String
--   (TyList TyInt) containing the read data.
checkRead :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates 'input(fd)'.
--   
--   Stream Input: Reads a line from a file descriptor (often used with 0
--   for stdin).
--   
--   <tt>param fd: Int (TyInt) the file descriptor to read from.
--   </tt>return: String (TyList TyInt) containing the input line.
checkInput :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

-- | Validates 'sizeof(arg)'.
--   
--   Returns the size (or length) of the argument. Accepts any type.
--   Returns an Integer.
--   
--   <tt>param arg: Any expression. </tt>return: Int (TyInt).
checkSizeof :: CheckExprFn -> CheckEnv -> [Ast] -> Either String Type

module AST.Semantics.Check

-- | Main entry point: validates AND transforms a list of AST nodes.
--   
--   This function iterates over the top-level AST nodes, threading the
--   environment state. It returns a new AST where <tt>auto</tt> types have
--   been resolved to concrete types.
--   
--   <tt>param asts: The list of raw AST nodes from the parser.
--   </tt>return: Either an error message or the transformed AST list.
checkAst :: [Ast] -> Either String [Ast]

-- | Check Expression: Verifies an expression and returns its Semantic
--   Type.
--   
--   Does not modify the AST, only extracts the type. Handles literals
--   (Int, Bool), variables (Symbol), and complex structures.
checkExpr :: CheckEnv -> Ast -> Either String Type

-- | Check Statement: Verifies AND transforms a statement.
--   
--   Dispatcher function that routes AST nodes to specific handlers.
--   Returns a tuple containing the transformed AST node (with inferred
--   types) and the updated environment.
--   
--   <tt>param env: Current Semantic Environment. </tt>param node: AST node
--   to process.
checkStmt :: CheckEnv -> Ast -> Either String (Ast, CheckEnv)

module Common.Utils.Bytecode.File

-- | Retrieves the file content or exits the program on error.
--   
--   @args - path: Path to the file.
--   
--   @details Handles the IO exception immediately: prints the error and
--   calls exitFailure. This prevents <tt>executeFile</tt> from handling
--   nested cases.
--   
--   @return The file content as ByteString.
getFileContent :: String -> IO ByteString

-- | Helper to attempt reading a file with explicit typing.
--   
--   @details Moves the type casting out of the main logic.
tryReadFile :: String -> IO (Either SomeException ByteString)

module Common.Utils.Bytecode.Header

-- | Validates the .gla file header and returns the raw bytecode.
--   
--   @details If the header is valid, drops the 10-byte header and returns
--   the code. If invalid, prints a generic error and exits.
extractContentIfValidHeader :: ByteString -> IO ByteString

-- | Evaluates the header validity by combining all predicates.
--   
--   @details Uses short-circuit boolean logic (&amp;&amp;). Order matters:
--   <a>hasValidSize</a> must be checked first to prevent segmentation
--   faults in <a>hasValidVersion</a>.
evaluateHeader :: ByteString -> Bool

-- | Checks if the file is large enough to contain a header (10 bytes).
hasValidSize :: ByteString -> Bool

-- | Checks if the Magic Number is <a>GLAD</a> (0x47 0x4C 0x41 0x44).
hasValidMagic :: ByteString -> Bool

-- | Checks if the Version is supported (0x02).
hasValidVersion :: ByteString -> Bool

module Common.Utils.List
listEq :: [a] -> [b] -> Bool
zipWith3M_ :: Monad m => (a -> b -> c -> m d) -> [a] -> [b] -> [c] -> m ()


-- | This module provides helper functions to encode primitive values into
--   binary form using <a>Builder</a>. These functions are used by the
--   assembler and encoder stages to produce the final bytecode stream.
--   
--   Supported encodings: - 32-bit signed integers (big-endian) - Single
--   bytes (Word8) - Booleans (encoded as 0 or 1) - UTF-8 strings with
--   length prefix
module Compiler.Bytecode.Encoder

-- | Encode a signed 32-bit integer in big-endian format.
--   
--   This function emits exactly 4 bytes corresponding to the given
--   <a>Int32</a> value, encoded in network byte order (big-endian).
--   
--   It is primarily used for instruction operands such as relative
--   offsets, indices, and immediate integer values.
encodeInt32BE :: Int32 -> Builder

-- | Encode a single byte.
--   
--   Writes the given <a>Word8</a> value as-is into the output stream. This
--   function is typically used to encode opcodes and small immediate
--   values.
encodeWord8 :: Word8 -> Builder

-- | Encode a boolean value as a single byte.
--   
--   Encoding convention:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><a>True</a> is encoded as <tt>1</tt></li>
--   <li><a>False</a> is encoded as <tt>0</tt></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   This representation is used consistently throughout the bytecode
--   format.
encodeBool :: Bool -> Builder

-- | Encode a UTF-8 string with a length prefix.
--   
--   The string is first encoded as UTF-8, then preceded by a 32-bit
--   big-endian integer representing the number of bytes in the encoded
--   string.
--   
--   Layout:
--   
--   <pre>
--   [length: Int32][utf8-bytes...]
--   </pre>
--   
--   This encoding is suitable for constant strings, symbol names, or
--   metadata embedded in the bytecode.
encodeString :: String -> Builder


module Compiler.Instruction

-- | The Instruction set used by compiler/VM
--   
--   @details Each constructor represents a single concrete virtual machine
--   instruction. Numeric opcodes and layout are defined in ASM_SPEC.md
--   (version 0x02).
--   
--   @return N/A (this documents the type)
data Instruction

-- | 0x01 PUSH [Type] [Value]
Push :: Immediate -> Instruction

-- | 0x02 POP
Pop :: Instruction

-- | 0x03 DUP
Dup :: Instruction

-- | 0x04 SWAP
Swap :: Instruction

-- | 0x10 ADD
Add :: Instruction

-- | 0x11 SUB
Sub :: Instruction

-- | 0x12 MUL
Mul :: Instruction

-- | 0x13 DIV
Div :: Instruction

-- | 0x14 MOD
Mod :: Instruction

-- | 0x20 EQ
Eq :: Instruction

-- | 0x26 TEQ
TEq :: Instruction

-- | 0x21 LT
Lt :: Instruction

-- | 0x25 LE
Le :: Instruction

-- | 0x22 NOT
Not :: Instruction

-- | 0x23 AND
And :: Instruction

-- | 0x24 OR
Or :: Instruction

-- | 0x30 JUMP [off]
Jump :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x31 JUMP_IF_FALSE [off]
JumpIfFalse :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x32 JUMP_IF_TRUE [off]
JumpIfTrue :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x40 CALL [off]
Call :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x41 TAILCALL [off]
TailCall :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x42 CALL_INDIRECT [address on stack]
CallIndirect :: Instruction

-- | 0x43 RET [stack size]
Ret :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x50 LOAD_LOCAL [idx]
LoadLocal :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x51 STORE_LOCAL [idx]
StoreLocal :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x52 LOAD_GLOBAL [idx]
LoadGlobal :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x53 STORE_GLOBAL [idx]
StoreGlobal :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x54 LOAD_CAPTURE [idx]
LoadCapture :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x55 STORE_CAPTURE [idx]
StoreCapture :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x60 MAKE_CLOSURE [addr] [n_captures]
MakeClosure :: Int -> Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x61 GET_FUNC_ADDR [id]
GetFuncAddr :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x62 BUILD_STRUCT [n_fields]
BuildStruct :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x63 GET_STRUCT_FIELD [idx]
GetStructField :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0x64 ATTR_UPDATE [struct] [idx] [value]
AttrUpdate :: Instruction

-- | 0x80 CAST [TypeID]
Cast :: Word8 -> Instruction

-- | 0x81 TYPEOF
TypeOf :: Instruction

-- | 0x82 SIZEOF
SizeOf :: Instruction

-- | 0x90 CONS
Cons :: Instruction

-- | 0x91 HEAD [list]
Head :: Instruction

-- | 0x92 TAIL [list]
Tail :: Instruction

-- | 0x93 NTH [list] [idx]
Nth :: Instruction

-- | 0x95 NTH_UPDATE [list] [idx] [value]
NthUpdate :: Instruction

-- | 0x94 BUILD_LIST [n_elements]
BuildList :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0xA0 OPEN
Open :: Instruction

-- | 0xA1 READ
Read :: Instruction

-- | 0xA2 WRITE
Write :: Instruction

-- | 0xA3 CLOSE
Close :: Instruction

-- | 0xA4 INPUT
Input :: Instruction

-- | 0x70 PRINT
Print :: Instruction

-- | 0x71 HALT
Halt :: Instruction

-- | 0x72 EXIT
Exit :: Instruction

-- | 0xFE CHECK_STACK [N]
CheckStack :: Int -> Instruction

-- | 0xFF NOP
Nop :: Instruction

-- | Immediate values pushed by PUSH.
--   
--   @details Immediate represents the different immediate payloads that
--   can be encoded after a PUSH opcode. The TypeID encoding follows
--   ASM_SPEC.md (version 0x02).
--   
--   @return N/A (this documents the type)
data Immediate

-- | TypeID 0x00
ImmBool :: Bool -> Immediate

-- | TypeID 0x01, 0x03, 0x05, 0x07 (i8..i64)
ImmInt :: IntValue -> Immediate

-- | Map an Immediate to the TypeID byte used by PUSH.
--   
--   @args - imm: the Immediate value whose TypeID is requested
--   
--   @details Returns the one-byte TypeID used by the binary format to
--   encode immediates as specified in the PUSH Type Table of ASM_SPEC.md.
--   
--   @return The TypeID as a <a>Word8</a>.
immediateToTypeID :: Immediate -> Word8

-- | Size in bytes of the immediate payload (not counting the TypeID byte).
--   
--   @args - imm: the Immediate whose payload size is requested
--   
--   @details This helper returns the number of bytes that follow the
--   TypeID for the immediate payload. It is useful for computing
--   instruction sizes and label offsets during assembly.
--   
--   @return The payload size in bytes as <a>Int</a>.
immediateSize :: Immediate -> Int

-- | Opcode mapping for each instruction as defined in doc/ASM_SPEC.md.
--   
--   @args - instr: the <a>Instruction</a> to map to its opcode byte
--   
--   @details This function centralizes the numeric opcode mapping,
--   ensuring the compiler and assembler use the same byte values when
--   serializing to the .gla format. It returns the opcode byte for a given
--   concrete instruction.
--   
--   @return The opcode as a <a>Word8</a>.
getInstCode :: Instruction -> Word8

-- | Computes the size in bytes of a given instruction, including its
--   payload.
--   
--   @args - instr: the <a>Instruction</a> whose size is to be computed
--   
--   @details Returns the total number of bytes required to encode the
--   instruction, including opcode and any immediate or address payloads.
--   Used for offset calculations and binary serialization.
--   
--   @return The instruction size in bytes as <a>Int</a>.
instructionSize :: Instruction -> Int
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Compiler.Instruction.Immediate
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Compiler.Instruction.Instruction
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Compiler.Instruction.Immediate
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Compiler.Instruction.Instruction
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Compiler.Instruction.Immediate
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Compiler.Instruction.Instruction

module Compiler.Bytecode.Serializer

-- | Serializes an <a>Instruction</a> to a <tt>Builder</tt> for binary
--   encoding.
--   
--   @args - instr: the <a>Instruction</a> to serialize
--   
--   @details Converts the instruction into its binary representation using
--   the appropriate opcode and payload encoding defined in ASM_SPEC.md.
--   
--   @return The encoded instruction as a <tt>Builder</tt>.
serializeInstruction :: Instruction -> Builder


-- | This module provides functionality to decode a binary bytecode stream
--   into a human-readable assembly format. It handles the complete
--   instruction set, including variable-length payloads, immediate values,
--   and system operations.
module Compiler.Bytecode.DisasmFinal

-- | Disassemble final bytecode into (offset, pretty-instruction) pairs.
--   
--   @args - bs: The raw ByteString containing the bytecode (header should
--   be stripped).
--   
--   @details This function runs the binary parser <a>disasmAll</a> over
--   the input string. It catches parsing errors (e.g., truncated files)
--   and returns a list of tuples containing the byte offset and the string
--   representation of the instruction.
--   
--   @return Either an error message (Text) or a list of (Offset,
--   InstructionString).
disasmFinal :: ByteString -> Either Text [(Int, String)]

module Compiler.ASM.Builtins

-- | Mapping of builtin operator names to their VM instructions.
builtinMap :: Map Text Instruction

-- | Helper to transform "[int]" to "int" or "[Point]" to <a>Point</a>
getInnerListType :: Text -> Either Text Text

-- | Returns the return type of a builtin based on its name and argument
--   types.
getBuiltinReturnType :: String -> [Text] -> Either Text Text


module Compiler.PsInstruction

-- | Pseudo-instructions used during compilation/assembly.
--   
--   @details PsInstruction is an intermediate representation used by the
--   compiler to express labels and label-referencing operations before a
--   dedicated assembly pass resolves textual labels to concrete
--   instruction offsets. Many constructors here resolve to a 'Real
--   Instruction' when labels are resolved in the assembly pass.
--   
--   @return N/A (this documents the type)
data PsInstruction

-- | A concrete instruction ready for bytecode generation
Real :: Instruction -> PsInstruction

-- | Defines a label position (e.g., "func_main:")
LabelDef :: Text -> PsInstruction

-- | Jumps to Label (resolved in assembly pass)
JumpLabel :: Text -> PsInstruction

-- | Resolves to Real (JumpIfFalse off)
JumpIfFalseLabel :: Text -> PsInstruction

-- | Resolves to Real (JumpIfTrue off)
JumpIfTrueLabel :: Text -> PsInstruction

-- | Function Calls to Label
CallLabel :: Text -> PsInstruction

-- | Resolves to Real (TailCall off)
TailCallLabel :: Text -> PsInstruction

-- | Closure &amp; Address Ops to Label Used when we need the address of a
--   function defined by a label
MakeClosureLabel :: Text -> Int -> PsInstruction

-- | Resolves to Real (GetFuncAddr off)
GetFuncAddrLabel :: Text -> PsInstruction
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Compiler.PsInstruction.PsInstruction
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Compiler.PsInstruction.PsInstruction


module Compiler.CompilerState

-- | Compiler state holding code buffers and symbol information.
--   
--   @details The CompilerState maintains two code buffers: <a>csCode</a>
--   for the current block being compiled (e.g., main or current function
--   body) and <a>csFuncs</a> for accumulating the code of defined
--   functions and lambdas that will be appended at the end of the binary.
--   
--   @return N/A (this documents the type)
data CompilerState
CompilerState :: Seq PsInstruction -> Seq PsInstruction -> SymTable -> Map Text [(Text, Text)] -> Int -> Int -> ScopeType -> Int -> [Text] -> CompilerState

-- | Generated code (in natural order)
[csCode] :: CompilerState -> Seq PsInstruction

-- | Compiled functions' buffer
[csFuncs] :: CompilerState -> Seq PsInstruction

-- | Local variable mapping
[csSymbols] :: CompilerState -> SymTable

-- | Struct definitions (Name -&gt; Field Names in order)
[csStructs] :: CompilerState -> Map Text [(Text, Text)]

-- | Next available local index
[csNextIndex] :: CompilerState -> Int

-- | Counter for unique label generation
[csLabelCnt] :: CompilerState -> Int

-- | Scope context (used to determine variables scopes)
[csScopeContext] :: CompilerState -> ScopeType

-- | Number of args on the stack (atomic return clean)
[csCurrentArgCount] :: CompilerState -> Int

-- | Stack of loop exit labels (for break)
[csLoopExits] :: CompilerState -> [Text]

-- | Symbol table mapping textual names to their scope and index.
--   
--   @details SymTable stores the mapping required to resolve variable
--   names to concrete memory indices. - ScopeType: Determines which LOAD
--   instruction to use. - MemoryIndex: The integer offset in the
--   stack/heap. - TypeName: The string representation of the variable's
--   type.
type SymTable = Map Text (ScopeType, Int, Text)

-- | Defines the memory scope of a variable.
--   
--   @details This enumeration is used in the symbol table to determine
--   which VM instruction (LOAD_GLOBAL, LOAD_LOCAL, or LOAD_CAPTURE) should
--   be emitted when a symbol is referenced.
data ScopeType

-- | Global variable (LOAD_GLOBAL)
ScopeGlobal :: ScopeType

-- | Local argument or variable (LOAD_LOCAL)
ScopeLocal :: ScopeType

-- | Variable captured by a closure (LOAD_CAPTURE)
ScopeCapture :: ScopeType

-- | Initial, empty compiler state.
--   
--   @details Provides a fresh CompilerState with no code, an empty symbol
--   table, the next local index set to 0 and the label counter set to 0.
--   
--   @return A <a>CompilerState</a> initialized for a new compilation unit.
createCompilerState :: CompilerState
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Compiler.CompilerState.CompilerState
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Compiler.CompilerState.ScopeType
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Compiler.CompilerState.CompilerState
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Compiler.CompilerState.ScopeType


module Compiler.ASM.CompilerMonad

-- | Compilation monad used throughout the compiler.
--   
--   @details CompilerMonad is a stateful monad carrying the
--   <a>CompilerState</a> and allowing early failure using 'Either Text'.
--   It is responsible for emitting pseudo- instructions, managing labels,
--   and updating compiler state consistently.
type CompilerMonad a = StateT CompilerState Either Text a

-- | Emit a concrete machine instruction.
--   
--   @args - instruction: the concrete <a>Instruction</a> to emit
--   
--   @details Wraps a real VM instruction into a <a>PsInstruction</a> and
--   appends it to the current code stream. This function is used for all
--   non-label bytecode instructions such as arithmetic, stack, and memory
--   operations.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
emitInstruction :: Instruction -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Define a label position in the emitted code.
--   
--   @args - labelName: textual name of the label
--   
--   @details Inserts a label definition at the current position in the
--   code stream. Labels are resolved later during the assembly pass into
--   concrete offsets.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
emitLabelDefinition :: Text -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Emit an unconditional jump to a label.
--   
--   @args - labelName: target label name
--   
--   @details Emits a pseudo-instruction representing an unconditional jump
--   whose destination will be resolved during the assembly phase.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
emitJumpToLabel :: Text -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Emit a conditional jump (jump if false) to a label.
--   
--   @args - labelName: target label name
--   
--   @details Emits a conditional jump that transfers control if the
--   boolean value on top of the stack evaluates to false. The actual jump
--   offset is resolved during assembly.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
emitJumpIfFalseToLabel :: Text -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Emit a conditional jump (jump if true) to a label.
--   
--   @args - labelName: target label name
--   
--   @details Emits a conditional jump that transfers control if the
--   boolean value on top of the stack evaluates to true. The actual jump
--   offset is resolved during assembly.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
emitJumpIfTrueToLabel :: Text -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Emit a function call to a label.
--   
--   @args - labelName: target function label
--   
--   @details Emits a pseudo-instruction representing a function call. The
--   label will be resolved to a concrete instruction offset during
--   assembly.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
emitCallToLabel :: Text -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Generate a unique label name using a given prefix.
--   
--   @args - prefixName: textual prefix for the generated label
--   
--   <tt>details Uses the internal <a>csLabelCnt</a> counter from
--   <a>CompilerState</a> to produce a unique label name of the form
--   </tt><a>prefix</a>_<a>n</a>@. The counter is incremented atomically as
--   part of the state update.
--   
--   @return A unique label name as <a>Text</a>.
generateUniqueLabel :: Text -> CompilerMonad Text

-- | Defines a new global symbol and allocates an index for it.
--   
--   @args - name: The name of the symbol to define. - tName: The type name
--   of the symbol to define.
--   
--   @details Checks if the symbol is already defined in <a>csSymbols</a>.
--   If it is, returns its current info. Otherwise, allocates the current
--   <a>csNextIndex</a>, inserts the symbol into the map, and increments
--   the index counter.
defineSymbol :: Text -> Text -> CompilerMonad (ScopeType, Int)

-- | Manually registers a symbol in the symbol table without code
--   generation.
--   
--   @args - name: Name of the symbol - tName: The type of the variable
--   (e.g., "int", <a>Player</a>) &lt;-- NOUVEAU - scopeType: The scope
--   type (Local, Global, or Capture) - idx: The specific memory index to
--   assign
--   
--   @details This function is used to populate the symbol table with
--   function arguments and captured variables before compiling a function
--   body. If the scope is <a>ScopeLocal</a> or <a>ScopeGlobal</a>, it also
--   updates <a>csNextIndex</a> to avoid collision. <a>ScopeCapture</a>
--   does not affect the index.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
registerSymbol :: Text -> Text -> ScopeType -> Int -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Registers a new structure definition in the compiler state.
--   
--   @args - name: The name of the structure. - fields: The list of field
--   names.
--   
--   @details Updates the <a>csStructs</a> map. If the structure is already
--   defined, it is overwritten (or you could raise an error depending on
--   desired behavior).
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
defineStruct :: Text -> [(Text, Text)] -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Retrieves the field names for a given structure.
--   
--   @args - name: The name of the structure to look up.
--   
--   @details Looks up the structure in the <a>csStructs</a> map. Returns
--   the list of fields if found, otherwise lifts a Left error.
--   
--   @return The list of field names wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>, or an
--   error.
getStructDefinition :: Text -> CompilerMonad [(Text, Text)]

-- | Retrieves the type name of an existing variable.
--   
--   @args - name: The variable name.
--   
--   @return The type string (e.g., <a>Player</a>) wrapped in
--   CompilerMonad. Throws an error if the variable is not defined.
getSymbolType :: Text -> CompilerMonad Text

-- | Retrieves all informations about a symbol.
lookupSymbol :: Text -> CompilerMonad (Maybe (ScopeType, Int, Text))

-- | Retreives index and type of a field within a specific structure.
--   
--   @args - structName: The name of the structure type (e.g.
--   <a>Player</a>). - fieldName: The name of the field to access (e.g.
--   "hp").
--   
--   @return (FieldIndex, FieldType)
getStructField :: Text -> Text -> CompilerMonad (Int, Text)

-- | Compiles an action within an isolated function scope.
--   
--   @args - compileAction: The monadic action to compile the function
--   body.
--   
--   @details This function creates an isolated environment (empty code
--   buffer, empty symbol table, reset index) to compile a function or
--   lambda. Once compiled, the generated code is moved to the
--   <a>csFuncs</a> buffer of the parent state, ensuring function code is
--   stored separately and not executed inline. Nested lambdas found during
--   compilation are also preserved.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileInIsolatedFunctionScope :: CompilerMonad () -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Append a pseudo-instruction to the current code sequence.
--   
--   @args - pseudoInst: the <a>PsInstruction</a> to append
--   
--   @details This internal helper mutates the compiler state by appending
--   the given pseudo-instruction to the end of the code buffer. The
--   underlying data structure is a <a>Seq</a>, allowing efficient O(1)
--   appends. This function is intentionally kept private to enforce
--   controlled emission.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
appendPseudoInstruction :: PsInstruction -> CompilerMonad ()


module Compiler.ASM.AstToAsm

-- | Pushes an Integer AST value directly to the stack.
--   
--   @args - val: The IntValue from the AST.
--   
--   @details Since the AST construction (Parser) already uses
--   <tt>fitInteger</tt> to determine the optimal storage size (I8, I16,
--   etc.), we simply wrap the value in an <a>ImmInt</a> and emit the PUSH
--   instruction.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
astIntToAsm :: IntValue -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Converts a native Haskell Bool to a PUSH instruction.
--   
--   @args - b: The boolean to convert.
--   
--   @details Emits a Push instruction with an immediate boolean value.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
astBoolToAsm :: Bool -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Converts a symbol (variable) to a LOAD instruction.
--   
--   @args - name: The name of the symbol.
--   
--   @details Looks up the symbol in the <a>csSymbols</a> table. Based on
--   the associated <a>ScopeType</a>, it emits either <a>LoadGlobal</a>,
--   <a>LoadLocal</a>, or <a>LoadCapture</a> with the correct index.
--   Returns an error if the symbol is undefined.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
astSymbolToAsm :: Text -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Converts a literal AST list to assembly instructions.
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - elements: The
--   list of AST nodes to compile.
--   
--   @details Compiles each element pushing them onto the stack, then calls
--   the builtin "list" function to construct the list object.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
astListToAsm :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> [Ast] -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a function call (Builtin or User-defined).
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - callee: The
--   AST representing the function being called. - args: The list of
--   argument ASTs.
--   
--   @details If the callee is a known builtin, emits the specific
--   instruction. Otherwise, emits a <tt>CallLabel</tt> to the named
--   function. (Higher-order calls are explicitly not supported in this
--   version).
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
astCallToAsm :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Ast -> [Ast] -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Mapping of builtin operator names to their VM instructions.
builtinMap :: Map Text Instruction


module Compiler.ASM.Compiler

-- | Main Dispatcher Function: Compiles any AST node.
--   
--   @args - ast: The AST node to compile.
--   
--   @details This is the central router of the compiler. It
--   pattern-matches on the AST constructors and delegates to the
--   appropriate specific compilation function. It passes itself
--   (<a>compileAst</a>) recursively to handle nested expressions.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileAst :: Ast -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a conditional expression (If-Then-Else).
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - cond: The
--   condition AST. - thenBranch: The AST for the True branch. -
--   elseBranch: The AST for the False branch.
--   
--   @details Generates labels for the Else block and the End. Emits
--   JumpIfFalse to skip the Then block if appropriate, and an
--   unconditional Jump to skip the Else block after executing Then.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileIf :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Ast -> Ast -> Ast -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a For loop.
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - initAst: The
--   initialization AST (executed once). - cond: The loop condition AST. -
--   updateAst: The update/increment AST (executed after each iteration). -
--   body: The loop body AST.
--   
--   @details Compiles the initialization step first. Then uses
--   <a>compileLoop</a> for the condition and body. Finally, compiles the
--   update step before jumping back.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileFor :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Ast -> Ast -> Ast -> Ast -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a While loop.
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - cond: The
--   loop condition AST. - body: The loop body AST.
--   
--   @details Generates start and end labels. Uses <a>compileLoop</a> for
--   the core logic and handles the looping jump back to start.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileWhile :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Ast -> Ast -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a variable definition.
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - name: The
--   name of the variable to define. - body: The expression to evaluate.
--   
--   @details Compiles the body to push the value onto the stack, allocates
--   a new global symbol index, and emits a StoreGlobal instruction.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileSetVar :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Text -> Text -> Ast -> Bool -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a structure instantiation.
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - name: The
--   name of the structure to instantiate. - assignedFields: The list of
--   (Field Name, Value AST) pairs.
--   
--   @details Retrieves the structure definition from <a>CompilerState</a>
--   using <a>getStructDefinition</a>. Reorders the provided values to
--   match the definition order, compiles them (pushing to stack), and
--   emits a <a>BuildStruct</a> instruction. Returns an error if the struct
--   is undefined or fields mismatch.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileSetStruct :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Text -> [(Text, Ast)] -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a named function definition.
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - name: The
--   function name. - args: The list of parameter names. - body: The
--   function body AST.
--   
--   @details Generates a label for the function and compiles the body
--   within an isolated function scope. Arguments are registered as
--   <a>ScopeLocal</a> symbols (indices 0 to N-1). The compiled code is
--   stored in <a>csFuncs</a>.
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileDefineFun :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Text -> [(Text, Text)] -> Ast -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a lambda definition.
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The main compilation function (recursion). -
--   params: List of parameter names. - body: The body of the lambda.
--   
--   @details 1. Identifies free variables (captures). 2. Emits code to
--   push captures onto the stack. 3. Generates a unique label for the
--   lambda body. 4. Compiles the body in an isolated scope. 5. Emits
--   <a>MakeClosure</a> to create the closure object at runtime.
compileDefineLambda :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> [Text] -> Ast -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Registers a structure definition.
--   
--   @args - name: The name of the structure. - fields: The list of (Field
--   Name, Field Type) pairs.
--   
--   @details Updates the <a>CompilerState</a> to store the list of field
--   names in order. No bytecode is emitted for a structure definition (it
--   is a compile-time metadata operation).
--   
--   @return Unit value wrapped in <a>CompilerMonad</a>.
compileDefineStruct :: Text -> [(Text, Text)] -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Helper function for Tail Call Optimization
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The standard compilation function for non-tail
--   expressions. - ast: The AST node to compile in tail position.
--   
--   @details Detects if the expression is a function call. If so, emits
--   <a>TailCallLabel</a> (TCO). If it is a control structure (If, List),
--   it propagates the tail context recursively. Otherwise, compiles
--   normally and emits <a>Ret</a>.
compileTail :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Ast -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Helper function to compile the common logic of loops.
--   
--   @args - compileFn: The recursive compilation function. - cond: The
--   condition AST. - body: The body AST. - lEnd: The label to jump to if
--   the condition is false.
--   
--   @details Compiles the condition, emits the jump-if-false check, and
--   compiles the body. This sequence is shared between While and For
--   loops.
compileLoop :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Ast -> Ast -> Text -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Compiles a struct field access.
--   
--   @details 1. Infers the type of the object being accessed (e.g.,
--   <a>Player</a>). 2. Looks up the field index in the struct definition.
--   3. Emits the code for the object followed by GET_STRUCT_FIELD.
compileAccessStruct :: (Ast -> CompilerMonad ()) -> Ast -> Text -> CompilerMonad ()

-- | Analyzes an AST node to find free variables (variables used but not
--   defined locally).
--   
--   @args - node: The AST node to analyze.
--   
--   @details Recursively traverses the AST to compute the set of free
--   variables. For a Lambda, free vars are (body_free_vars - parameters).
--   For a Define, the defined name is excluded from the body's free vars.
--   This function is critical for determining closure captures. Built-in
--   operators (like +, -, *) are excluded from free variables.
--   
--   @return A Set of Text representing the names of free variables.
getLambdaFreeVariables :: Ast -> Set Text

-- | Infers the type of an AST expression.
--   
--   @details - ASymbol: Look up the variable in the symbol table. -
--   AAccessStruct: Recursively infer the parent object's type, then look
--   up the field's type.
inferType :: Ast -> CompilerMonad Text

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.ResolveLabelsHelpers
checkInt32Range :: Int64 -> Either Text Int32
computeOffset :: Int -> Int -> Int64
sizeOfJumpInst :: Int
sizeOfJumpIfFalseInst :: Int
sizeOfJumpIfTrueInst :: Int
sizeOfCallInst :: Int
sizeOfTailCallInst :: Int

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2CallLabel
step2CallLabel :: Map Text Int -> Set Int -> [Instruction] -> Int -> Text -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2GetFuncAddrLabel
step2GetFuncAddrLabel :: Map Text Int -> Set Int -> [Instruction] -> Int -> Text -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2JumpIfFalseLabel
step2JumpIfFalseLabel :: Map Text Int -> Set Int -> [Instruction] -> Int -> Text -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2JumpIfTrueLabel
step2JumpIfTrueLabel :: Map Text Int -> Set Int -> [Instruction] -> Int -> Text -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2JumpLabel
step2JumpLabel :: Map Text Int -> Set Int -> [Instruction] -> Int -> Text -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2LabelDef
step2LabelDef :: [Instruction] -> Int -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2MakeClosureLabel
step2MakeClosureLabel :: Map Text Int -> Set Int -> [Instruction] -> Int -> Text -> Int -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2Real
step2Real :: [Instruction] -> Int -> Instruction -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.Step2TailCallLabel
step2TailCallLabel :: Map Text Int -> Set Int -> [Instruction] -> Int -> Text -> Either Text ([Instruction], Int)

module Compiler.ResolveLabels.ResolveLabels
resolveLabels :: [PsInstruction] -> Either Text [Instruction]

module Compiler.ASM.Assembler

-- | Main assembly function.
--   
--   @details 1. Resolves labels (PsInstruction -&gt; Instruction) using
--   ResolveLabels module. 2. Validates jump offsets (bounds checking). 3.
--   Serializes instructions to ByteString with Header.
assemble :: [PsInstruction] -> Either Text ByteString


-- | This module defines the basic building blocks for the parser,
--   including: - Space consumers (handling whitespace and comments) -
--   Lexeme wrappers - Symbol and keyword parsers - Reserved words
--   management
module Parser.Lexer

-- | The standard Parser type for this project.
--   
--   It uses Void as the custom error component (no custom errors) and
--   DT.Text as the input stream type.
type Parser = Parsec Void Text

-- | Space Consumer.
--   
--   Consumes whitespace and ignores comments. Supported comment styles:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>Line comments starting with //</li>
--   <li>Block comments enclosed in <i>* ... *</i></li>
--   </ul>
sc :: Parser ()

-- | Wrapper for lexemes.
--   
--   Consumes trailing whitespace after parsing the given parser
--   <tt>p</tt>. This is essential for the "trailing whitespace" convention
--   used in this parser.
lexeme :: Parser a -> Parser a

-- | Parse a fixed string as a symbol.
--   
--   Consumes the string exactly as matches, followed by whitespace.
symbol :: Text -> Parser Text

-- | Parse a specific keyword.
--   
--   Ensures that the keyword is not followed by an alphanumeric character
--   to prevent partial matches (e.g., matching "if" inside "ifelse").
pKeyword :: Text -> Parser Text

-- | Parse a valid identifier.
--   
--   An identifier must start with a letter or underscore, followed by
--   alphanumeric characters or underscores.
--   
--   It fails if the parsed identifier is one of the <a>reservedWords</a>.
pIdentifier :: Parser Text

-- | Parse content between parentheses (...).
parens :: Parser a -> Parser a

-- | Parse content between braces {...}.
braces :: Parser a -> Parser a

-- | Parse a semicolon ; symbol.
semicolon :: Parser Text

-- | Parse a comma , symbol.
comma :: Parser Text

-- | Parse a colon : symbol.
colon :: Parser Text

-- | Wraps a parser with position information.
--   
--   Captures the current source position (line, column) before running the
--   parser <tt>p</tt>, and wraps the resulting AST node in an <a>APos</a>
--   constructor. This allows error reporting to pinpoint the exact
--   location of semantic errors later.
--   
--   <tt>param Parser Ast The parser to wrap. </tt>return Parser Ast A
--   parser that returns an APos node containing the original result.
withPos :: Parser Ast -> Parser Ast


-- | This module handles the parsing of values and expressions using
--   <a>makeExprParser</a>. It supports: - Integers, Booleans, Strings,
--   Chars, Lists - Variables and Function calls - Operator precedence
--   (PEMDAS, etc.)
module Parser.Expression

-- | Main expression parser.
--   
--   Uses <a>makeExprParser</a> to handle operator precedence and
--   associativity automatically.
pExpr :: Parser Ast


-- | This module defines parsers for control flow: - Conditional statements
--   (if/else) - Iteration statements (while) Note: Parsers in this module
--   often require <tt>pBlock</tt> and <tt>pVarDef</tt> as arguments to
--   avoid circular dependencies with Parser.Statement.
module Parser.Conditions

-- | Parse a full conditional statement: if, else if, else.
--   
--   This function uses Dependency Injection for <tt>pVarDef</tt> and
--   <tt>pBlock</tt>.
pIf :: Parser Ast -> Parser Ast -> Parser Ast

-- | Parse a while loop.
--   
--   Syntax: while (condition) { body } The body parsing relies on the
--   injected <tt>pBlockParam</tt>.
pWhile :: Parser Ast -> Parser Ast

-- | Parse a for loop.
--   
--   Syntax: for (init; cond; update) { body } The condition is mandatory
--   to prevent infinite loops by accident.
pFor :: Parser Ast -> Parser Ast -> Parser Ast


-- | This module defines parsers for the structural elements of the
--   language: - Variable definitions - Function declarations - Return
--   statements - Type annotations - Code blocks
module Parser.Statement

-- | Main entry point for the parser.
--   
--   Parses a list of statements from the input text until EOF. The
--   filename argument is used for error reporting.
parseALL :: Text -> Either (ParseErrorBundle Text Void) [Ast]

-- | Main statement parser.
--   
--   Aggregates all statement types (control flow, declarations, basic
--   instructions) into a single choice. This is the top-level parser for a
--   line of code.
pStatement :: Parser Ast

module Parser.ImportSystem

-- | Main entry point used by the Compiler/VM. Resolves all <a>AImport</a>
--   nodes within a list of AST statements.
--   
--   <tt>param asts: The initial list of AST nodes (parsed from the main
--   file). </tt>return: Either an error message (String) or the fully
--   resolved AST list.
resolveImports :: [Ast] -> IO (Either String [Ast])

-- | Helper used by unit tests to reconstruct AFor nodes.
constructForAst :: [Ast] -> Either String [Ast]

module VM.VMValue

-- | Represents a runtime value within the Virtual Machine.
--   
--   @details This data structure encompasses all possible types that can
--   exist on the stack or in memory during the execution of the program.
--   It bridges the gap between the static AST and the dynamic runtime.
data VMValue

-- | Represents an integer value (wrapping the Common IntValue type). Used
--   for all arithmetic operations.
VInt :: IntValue -> VMValue

-- | Represents a boolean value (#t or #f). Used for logic operations and
--   conditional jumps.
VBool :: Bool -> VMValue

-- | Represents a dynamic list of values. Corresponds to the <tt>AList</tt>
--   node in the AST.
VList :: Vector VMValue -> VMValue

-- | Represents an instance of a structure. Fields are stored contiguously.
--   The compiler resolves field names to indices.
VStruct :: Vector VMValue -> VMValue

-- | Represents a closure (anonymous function with captured context).
--   <tt>param Int The absolute instruction pointer address of the function
--   code. </tt>param Vector The captured environment (free variables) from
--   the creation scope.
VClosure :: Int -> Vector VMValue -> VMValue

-- | Represents a raw function pointer without captured variables. @param
--   Int The absolute instruction pointer address.
VFuncPtr :: Int -> VMValue

-- | Represents the absence of a value (Unit/Null). Used for functions that
--   do not return data.
VVoid :: VMValue

-- | Recursively determines the precise type name of a value.
--   
--   <tt>arg val: The VMValue to inspect. </tt>return The formatted type
--   string (e.g., "[int]", <a>Player</a>, "[[char]]").
--   
--   @details - Primitives: Returns "int", "bool", "void". - Chars:
--   Distinguished from Ints via IChar/UIChar -&gt; "char". - Structs:
--   Returns the stored name (e.g., <a>Player</a>). - Lists: Recursively
--   inspects the *first* element to build the type syntax. [] -&gt;
--   "[void]" [1, 2] -&gt; "[int]" ["hi"] -&gt; "[[char]]"
getValueName :: VMValue -> Text

-- | Converts a VMValue to a specific target TypeID.
--   
--   @args - typeId: The target type identifier (see ASM_SPEC). - val: The
--   value to convert.
--   
--   @details Performs a native conversion (truncation or extension) via
--   <a>fromIntegral</a>. Supports converting between Booleans, Integers
--   (signed/unsigned) and Chars.
castValue :: Word8 -> VMValue -> VMValue

-- | Converts a VMValue into a human-readable Text representation.
--   
--   <tt>param val The value to convert. </tt>return A Text representing
--   the value.
--   
--   @details This function handles type-specific formatting: - **Chars**:
--   Converted to single-character strings. - **Lists**: If the list
--   contains only Characters, it is rendered as a raw string (e.g.,
--   <a>Hello</a>). Otherwise, it uses list notation (e.g., "[1, 2, #t]").
--   - **Structs**: Rendered with curly braces (e.g., "{10, 20}"). -
--   **Bools**: Rendered as #t or #f (Scheme style).
valueToString :: VMValue -> Text

-- | Helper to extract a raw integer value for casting purposes.
--   
--   @details - Integers: returns the raw value. - Booleans: True -&gt; 1,
--   False -&gt; 0. - Pointers: returns the address. - Others: returns 0
--   (safe default).
valueToInt :: VMValue -> Int

-- | Recursive equality check for VMValues.
--   
--   @details Handles loose integer comparison inside Lists and Structs.
--   e.g., [I8 5] == [I64 5] returns True.
eqValue :: VMValue -> VMValue -> Bool

-- | Converts a Text string into a VMValue.
--   
--   @arg txt: The text string to convert.
--   
--   @details Transforms the Text into a VList of VInt (IChar). This
--   reverses the logic of <a>valueToString</a> for strings, creating the
--   standard list-based string representation used by the VM.
stringToValue :: Text -> VMValue

-- | Converts a single Character to a VMValue.
--   
--   @arg c: The character to convert.
--   
--   @details Wraps the character's ordinal value into an IChar (Int8).
--   Used as a helper for string conversion.
charToValue :: Char -> VMValue
instance GHC.Classes.Eq VM.VMValue.VMValue
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show VM.VMValue.VMValue

module VM.CallSnapshot

-- | Represents a single frame in the call stack.
--   
--   @details A CallSnapshot is pushed onto the call stack whenever a
--   function is called. It acts as a checkpoint, storing the context of
--   the caller so the VM can restore it when the called function returns.
data CallSnapshot
CallSnapshot :: Int -> Int -> Vector VMValue -> CallSnapshot

-- | The address (ByteString index) where execution should resume after the
--   current function returns.
[callbackIndex] :: CallSnapshot -> Int

-- | The value of the Frame Pointer before the call. This is essential to
--   restore the caller's view of its local variables.
[vStackIndex] :: CallSnapshot -> Int

-- | The environment captured by the closure being executed. Allows the
--   function to access variables defined outside its body but available at
--   definition time.
[vEnv] :: CallSnapshot -> Vector VMValue
instance GHC.Classes.Eq VM.CallSnapshot.CallSnapshot
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show VM.CallSnapshot.CallSnapshot

module VM.VMState

-- | The core state of the Virtual Machine.
--   
--   @details This structure holds the entire context of the executing
--   program at any given microsecond. It includes memory (stack,
--   heap/globals), the processor registers (IP, FP), and the code itself.
data VMState
VMState :: ByteString -> Int -> Vector VMValue -> Int -> [CallSnapshot] -> Vector VMValue -> Vector VMValue -> Bool -> Bool -> Map Int Handle -> Int -> VMState

-- | The read-only byte array containing the compiled machine code.
[bytecode] :: VMState -> ByteString

-- | The current index in <a>bytecode</a>. When a function is called, this
--   value (plus offset) becomes the <a>callbackIndex</a> in the pushed
--   CallSnapshot.
[bytecodeIndex] :: VMState -> Int

-- | The main data stack. Contains inputs, outputs, and local variables.
[vStack] :: VMState -> Vector VMValue

-- | The index in <a>vStack</a> where the current function's local
--   variables begin. When a function is called, this value is saved as
--   <a>vStackIndex</a> in the CallSnapshot.
[baseVStackIndex] :: VMState -> Int

-- | The stack of saved contexts (formerly callStack). Used to restore the
--   state upon returning from a function.
[snapshotStack] :: VMState -> [CallSnapshot]

-- | The Current Environment (Closures). Contains variables captured by the
--   currently executing function. If the current function is not a
--   closure, this is typically empty.
[env] :: VMState -> Vector VMValue

-- | The persistent global environment. Stores global variables accessible
--   throughout the program life.
[globalEnv] :: VMState -> Vector VMValue

-- | Execution flag. If False, the VM loop terminates.
[isRunning] :: VMState -> Bool

-- | Enable tracing
[isDebug] :: VMState -> Bool

-- | Table of file descriptors (Kernel)
[vmFds] :: VMState -> Map Int Handle

-- | Next free fd
[nextFd] :: VMState -> Int

-- | The Monad Transformer stack used for the VM.
--   
--   @details We use <a>StateT</a> to carry the <a>VMState</a> and
--   <a>IO</a> to allow for side effects like printing to the console
--   (PRINT instruction).
type VirtualMachine a = StateT VMState IO a

-- | Creates the initial state of the VM for a given program.
--   
--   @args - code: The compiled binary code to execute.
--   
--   @return A pristine <a>VMState</a> ready for execution.
createVMState :: ByteString -> Bool -> VMState

-- | Creates a snapshot of the current VM context (IP, FP, Env).
--   
--   @args - vm: The current VM state.
--   
--   @details Captures the current Instruction Pointer, Frame Pointer, and
--   Closure Environment. Used by CALL instructions to save the state
--   before jumping.
--   
--   @return A <a>CallSnapshot</a> containing the saved context.
createSnapshot :: VMState -> CallSnapshot

-- | Sets up a new stack frame for a function call (Shared Logic).
--   
--   @args - idx: The absolute address (index) to jump to. - newEnv: The
--   closure environment to load (empty for static calls).
--   
--   @details 1. Creates and pushes a snapshot of the current state. 2.
--   Updates FP (baseVStackIndex) and IP (bytecodeIndex). 3. Sets the new
--   environment.
--   
--   @return Unit. State is modified.
doSnapshot :: Int -> Vector VMValue -> VirtualMachine ()


-- | This module provides the core abstractions to interact with the VM's
--   operand stack. It abstracts the underlying <tt>Vector</tt>
--   implementation and handles underflow safety checks.
module VM.VMStack

-- | Pushes a value onto the top of the global value stack.
--   
--   @args - val: The <a>VMValue</a> to push.
--   
--   @details Modifies the VM state by appending the value to the end of
--   the <a>vStack</a> vector. This operation is generally O(1).
stackPush :: VMValue -> VirtualMachine ()

-- | Removes and returns the value at the top of the stack.
--   
--   @details Retrieves the last element of the <a>vStack</a> vector and
--   removes it from the state. Uses 'case' instead of 'if' to avoid
--   DoAndIfThenElse extension.
--   
--   @throws Error "VM Error: Stack Underflow" if the stack is empty.
--   
--   @return The <a>VMValue</a> that was at the top.
stackPop :: VirtualMachine VMValue

-- | Returns the value at the top of the stack without removing it (Peek).
--   
--   @details Useful for instructions like DUP or conditional jumps that
--   need to inspect the value without consuming it.
--   
--   @throws Error "VM Error: Stack Underflow (Top)" if the stack is empty.
--   
--   @return The <a>VMValue</a> currently at the top.
stackTop :: VirtualMachine VMValue


module VM.Instruction.Logic

-- | Implements Equality Comparison (Opcode 0x20).
--   
--   @details Pops two values and performs a deep equality check. Supports:
--   Ints (loose), Bools, Lists (recursive), Structs, FuncPtrs.
instEq :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Typed Equality (Strict ===).
--   
--   @details Checks if two values are identical in Type AND Value. No
--   implicit casting (I8 5 !== I64 5). Standard Haskell <a>==</a> on
--   VMValue does exactly this.
instTEq :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Less Than Comparison (Opcode 0x21).
--   
--   @details Pops two values and checks if the second popped (Left) is
--   less than the first (Right). Stack: [a, b] -&gt; [a &lt; b] (Push
--   VBool)
instLt :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Less or Equal Comparison (Opcode 0x25).
--   
--   @details Pops two integers and checks if Left &lt;= Right. Stack: [a,
--   b] -&gt; [a &lt;= b]
instLe :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Logical NOT (Opcode 0x22).
--   
--   @details Pops a boolean and pushes its inverse. Stack: [a] -&gt; [not
--   a]
--   
--   @throws Error if the popped value is not a VBool.
instNot :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Logical AND (Opcode 0x23).
--   
--   @details Pops two booleans and pushes their conjunction. Stack: [a, b]
--   -&gt; [a &amp;&amp; b]
instAnd :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Logical OR (Opcode 0x24).
--   
--   @details Pops two booleans and pushes their disjunction. Stack: [a, b]
--   -&gt; [a || b]
instOr :: VirtualMachine ()


-- | This module implements low-level file system interactions (Open, Read,
--   Write, Close). It acts as a bridge between the VM's stack-based memory
--   and the Host OS.
module VM.Instruction.Io

-- | Implements OPEN instruction (Opcode 0xB0).
--   
--   <tt>arg StackTop: Mode (Int) - 0:Read, 1:Write, 2:Append. </tt>arg
--   StackNext: Path (String).
--   
--   @details Pops path and mode, calls tryOpen, and pushes the resulting
--   FD. Safety: Returns -1 on failure instead of crashing.
instOpen :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements READ instruction (Opcode 0xB1).
--   
--   <tt>arg StackTop: Size (Int). </tt>arg StackNext: FD (Int).
--   
--   @details Reads <tt>Size</tt> bytes from the file descriptor
--   <tt>FD</tt>. Pushes the read content string to the stack.
instRead :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements WRITE instruction (Opcode 0xB2).
--   
--   <tt>arg StackTop: Content (String). </tt>arg StackNext: FD (Int).
--   
--   @details Writes content to the specified file descriptor. Ignores
--   operation if FD is invalid.
instWrite :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements CLOSE instruction (Opcode 0xB3).
--   
--   @arg StackTop: FD (Int).
--   
--   @details Closes the handle and removes the FD from the VM state map.
--   Safe to call on invalid FD (no-op).
instClose :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements INPUT instruction (Opcode 0xB4).
--   
--   @arg StackTop: FD (Int).
--   
--   @details Reads a single line from the FD (useful for stdin). Pushes
--   the string content (without newline usually) to stack.
instInput :: VirtualMachine ()


-- | Handles basic arithmetic. WARNING: Operations are performed on the top
--   two stack elements. Since the stack is LIFO, the first popped element
--   is the Right-Hand Operand.
module VM.Instruction.Arithmetic

-- | Implements Addition (Opcode 0x10).
--   
--   Stack: [a, b] -&gt; [a + b]
instAdd :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Subtraction (Opcode 0x11).
--   
--   Stack: [a, b] -&gt; [a - b] (Note: b is popped first)
instSub :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Multiplication (Opcode 0x12).
--   
--   Stack: [a, b] -&gt; [a * b]
instMul :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Division (Opcode 0x13).
--   
--   Stack: [a, b] -&gt; [a / b]
instDiv :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Modulo (Opcode 0x14).
--   
--   Stack: [a, b] -&gt; [a % b]
instMod :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Helper function for binary integer operations.
--   
--   @args - fn: The Haskell binary function to apply (e.g., (+), (-)).
--   
--   @details 1. Pops the Right Operand (v2). 2. Pops the Left Operand
--   (v1). 3. Checks if both are integers. 4. Applies <tt>fn</tt> and
--   pushes the result.
--   
--   @throws Error if operands are not VInt.
binaryInstInt :: (Int -> Int -> Int) -> VirtualMachine ()

-- | Helper function for division and modulo with Zero Check.
--   
--   @args - fn: The Haskell binary function (div or mod).
--   
--   @throws Error "VM Error: Division by Zero" if the divisor (v2) is 0.
binaryInstIntZero :: (Int -> Int -> Int) -> VirtualMachine ()


-- | This module provides low-level functions to consume bytes from the
--   VM's bytecode stream. It supports reading signed and unsigned integers
--   of 8, 16, 32, and 64 bits in Big Endian format (Network Byte Order).
module VM.Bytecode.Reader

-- | Reads a single raw byte (8 bits) from the bytecode.
--   
--   @details Retrieves the byte at the current <a>bytecodeIndex</a> and
--   increments the index. Performs a bounds check to prevent reading past
--   the end of the bytecode.
--   
--   @throws Error "VM Error: Unexpected End of Bytecode" if the index is
--   out of bounds.
--   
--   @return The read <a>Word8</a>.
readByte :: VirtualMachine Word8

-- | Reads a signed 8-bit integer.
--   
--   @return The value as <a>Int8</a>.
readInt8 :: VirtualMachine Int8

-- | Reads an unsigned 8-bit integer.
--   
--   @return The value as <a>Word8</a>.
readWord8 :: VirtualMachine Word8

-- | Reads a signed 16-bit integer (Big Endian).
--   
--   @return The value as <a>Int16</a>.
readInt16 :: VirtualMachine Int16

-- | Reads an unsigned 16-bit integer (Big Endian).
--   
--   @return The value as <a>Word16</a>.
readWord16 :: VirtualMachine Word16

-- | Reads a signed 32-bit integer (Big Endian) and returns it as a native
--   <a>Int</a>.
--   
--   @details This function is optimized for general usage (like jumping or
--   vector indexing). It reads 4 bytes, interprets them as a signed Int32,
--   and casts to the native <a>Int</a> type. On 64-bit systems, this
--   preserves the sign correctly.
--   
--   @return The value as a standard <a>Int</a>.
readInt32 :: VirtualMachine Int

-- | Reads an unsigned 32-bit integer (Big Endian).
--   
--   @return The value as <a>Word32</a>.
readWord32 :: VirtualMachine Word32

-- | Reads a signed 64-bit integer (Big Endian).
--   
--   @return The value as <a>Int64</a>.
readInt64 :: VirtualMachine Int64

-- | Reads an unsigned 64-bit integer (Big Endian).
--   
--   @return The value as <a>Word64</a>.
readWord64 :: VirtualMachine Word64


-- | Handles LOAD_LOCAL and STORE_LOCAL operations. These instructions
--   access the stack relative to the current Frame Pointer (FP). This
--   allows functions to access their arguments (negative offsets) and
--   local variables (positive offsets) regardless of the absolute stack
--   depth.
module VM.Instruction.Variable

-- | Implements LOAD_LOCAL (Opcode 0x50).
--   
--   @details 1. Reads the signed 32-bit index (offset) from the bytecode.
--   2. Calculates the absolute index: Frame Pointer (FP) + Offset. 3.
--   Copies the value at that index to the top of the stack.
--   
--   This instruction is used to retrieve arguments and local variables.
--   
--   @throws Error "VM Error: LOAD_LOCAL out of bounds" if the calculated
--   index is outside the valid stack range.
instLoadLocal :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements STORE_LOCAL (Opcode 0x51).
--   
--   @details 1. Reads the relative index. 2. Pops the value to store. 3.
--   Calculates the absolute index (FP + offset). 4. Delegates to
--   <a>updateLocalVar</a> to handle stack growth or update.
instStoreLocal :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements LOAD_CAPTURE (Opcode 0x54).
--   
--   @details Accesses a variable in the current function's captured
--   environment. 1. Reads the capture index (Int32). 2. Pushes the value
--   at 'env[index]' onto the stack.
instLoadCapture :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements STORE_CAPTURE (Opcode 0x55).
--   
--   @details Updates a variable in the current function's captured
--   environment. 1. Reads the capture index. 2. Pops the new value. 3.
--   Writes to 'env[index]'.
instStoreCapture :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements LOAD_GLOBAL (Opcode 0x52).
--   
--   @details Accesses the Global Environment (Heap) at the given index.
instLoadGlobal :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements STORE_GLOBAL (Opcode 0x53).
--   
--   @details Stores the top of the stack into the Global Environment at
--   <tt>idx</tt>.
instStoreGlobal :: VirtualMachine ()


module VM.Instruction.System

-- | Implements PRINT (Opcode 0x70).
--   
--   @details Pops the top value from the stack and prints its string
--   representation to the standard output (stdout), followed by a newline.
--   Useful for debugging or simple output programs.
instPrint :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements HALT (Opcode 0x71).
--   
--   @details Sets the <a>isRunning</a> flag of the VM state to False. This
--   will cause the main Execution loop to terminate gracefully on the next
--   cycle.
instHalt :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements EXIT (Opcode 0x72).
--   
--   @details Pops an integer status code from the stack and terminates the
--   process. Useful for unit testing (exit 84 on failure).
instExit :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements CHECK_STACK (Opcode 0xFE).
--   
--   @details Ensures the stack has at least <tt>N</tt> elements. Reads
--   <tt>N</tt> as an Int32. Throws error if stack is too small.
instCheckStack :: VirtualMachine ()


-- | Handles the creation of structures.
module VM.Instruction.Struct

-- | Implements BUILD_STRUCT (Opcode 0x62).
--   
--   @details Pop <tt>n</tt> elements from the stack and wraps them in a
--   VStruct. 1. Reads <tt>n</tt> (Int32). 2. Consumes <tt>n</tt> values.
--   3. Pushes VStruct.
instBuildStruct :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements GET_STRUCT_FIELD (Opcode 0x63).
--   
--   @details Reads a field index and retrieves the value from a Struct on
--   the stack. 1. Reads <tt>index</tt> (Int32). 2. Pops <tt>struct</tt>
--   (VStruct). 3. Pushes 'struct[index]'.
--   
--   @throws Error if the popped value is not a VStruct or if index is out
--   of bounds.
instGetStructField :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements ATTR_UPDATE (Opcode 0x64).
--   
--   @details Updates a field in a structure. Because structures are
--   immutable, this creates a shallow copy.
--   
--   Stack Order: Top -&gt; New Value Next -&gt; Field Index (Int) Bottom
--   -&gt; Struct
instAttrUpdate :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Helper for instBuildStruct to manipulate the stack.
--   
--   @args - vm: Current VM state - count: Number of fields in the struct
pushStruct :: VMState -> Int -> VirtualMachine ()


-- | Handles instructions that modify the stack structure itself (PUSH,
--   POP, DUP). This module relies on <a>BytecodeReader</a> to decode
--   operands of varying sizes.
module VM.Instruction.Stack

-- | Implements the PUSH instruction (Opcode 0x01).
--   
--   @details This is the entry point for the PUSH operation. It performs
--   the following steps: 1. Reads the **TypeID** byte from the bytecode
--   stream. 2. Delegates the reading of the value and the stack push to
--   <a>stackPushValue</a>.
--   
--   This separation allows for a cleaner implementation and easier
--   extension of supported types in the future.
instPush :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements the POP instruction (Opcode 0x02).
--   
--   @details Removes the top element of the stack and discards it.
--   Commonly used to clean up the stack after an expression evaluation
--   where the result is not needed (e.g., `func();` where return is
--   ignored).
--   
--   @throws Error "Stack Underflow" if the stack is empty.
instPop :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements the DUP instruction (Opcode 0x03).
--   
--   @details Duplicates the top element of the stack. Useful for
--   operations that consume a value but need to preserve it for a
--   subsequent operation. State change: `[..., A] -&gt; [..., A, A]`
--   
--   @throws Error "Stack Underflow" if the stack is empty.
instDup :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements the SWAP instruction (Opcode 0x04).
--   
--   @details Swaps the top two elements of the stack. Stack: [..., A, B]
--   -&gt; [..., B, A]
instSwap :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements CAST (Opcode 0x80).
--   
--   @details Reads a TypeID and tries to convert the top of stack to that
--   type.
instCast :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements TYPEOF (Opcode 0x81).
--   
--   @details Pops a value from the stack, determines its runtime type, and
--   pushes a string representation (e.g., "int", "list").
--   
--   Stack: [value] -&gt; ["type_name"]
instTypeOf :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements SIZEOF (Opcode 0x82).
--   
--   @details Pops a value and pushes its length. - List: Number of
--   elements. - Struct: Number of fields. - Others: 0 (or error, depending
--   on strictness choice).
--   
--   @throws Error if the value is not a container (List/Struct).
instSizeOf :: VirtualMachine ()

module VM.Instruction.List

-- | Implements CONS (Opcode 0x90).
--   
--   @details Constructs a new list by prepending an element. Stack: [...,
--   elem, list] -&gt; [..., new_list] Note: Pops <tt>list</tt> first
--   (Right), then <a>elem</a> (Left).
instCons :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements HEAD (Opcode 0x91).
--   
--   @details Extracts the first element of a list. Stack: [..., list]
--   -&gt; [..., head]
--   
--   @throws Error if list is empty.
instHead :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements TAIL (Opcode 0x92).
--   
--   @details Extracts the rest of the list (minus the first element).
--   Stack: [..., list] -&gt; [..., tail]
--   
--   @throws Error if list is empty.
instTail :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements NTH (Opcode 0x93).
--   
--   @details Access to a list element. Stack: [index, list] -&gt;
--   [element]
instNth :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements NTH_UPDATE (Opcode 0x95).
--   
--   @details Updates an element in a list at a given index. Note: Since
--   VMValues are immutable, this pushes a NEW list.
--   
--   Stack Order (arg order: list, index, value): Top -&gt; Value Next
--   -&gt; Index Bottom -&gt; List
instNthUpdate :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements BUILD_LIST (Opcode 0x94).
--   
--   @details Pop <tt>n</tt> elements from the stack and creates a VList.
--   Preserves the order: [e1, e2] -&gt; push e1 -&gt; push e2 -&gt;
--   BuildList 2 -&gt; VList [e1, e2]
instBuildList :: VirtualMachine ()


-- | Handles relative jumps and conditional branching instructions. These
--   instructions modify the <a>bytecodeIndex</a> (Instruction Pointer) of
--   the VMState.
module VM.Instruction.Index

-- | Implements Unconditional Jump (Opcode 0x30).
--   
--   @details 1. Reads a signed 32-bit integer (offset) from the bytecode.
--   2. Adds this offset to the current <a>bytecodeIndex</a>.
--   
--   Note: Since <a>readInt32</a> advances the index by 4 bytes, the offset
--   is effectively relative to the instruction immediately following the
--   JUMP.
instJump :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Jump If False (Opcode 0x31).
--   
--   @details Conditional jump used for 'if' statements and loops. 1. Reads
--   the jump offset. 2. Pops a value from the stack. 3. If the value is
--   'VBool False', applies the jump. 4. If 'VBool True', continues
--   execution normally (fall-through).
--   
--   @throws Error "VM Error: JUMP_IF_FALSE expects Boolean" if the popped
--   value is not a boolean.
instJumpIfFalse :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements Jump If True (Opcode 0x32).
--   
--   @details Conditional jump (reverse logic of JumpIfFalse). 1. Reads the
--   jump offset. 2. Pops a value from the stack. 3. If the value is 'VBool
--   True', applies the jump.
--   
--   @throws Error "VM Error: JUMP_IF_TRUE expects Boolean" if the popped
--   value is not a boolean.
instJumpIfTrue :: VirtualMachine ()


-- | Handles the creation and destruction of stack frames (CallSnapshots).
--   Ensures proper scope management and control flow between functions.
module VM.Instruction.Function

-- | Implements CALL (Opcode 0x40).
--   
--   @details Static call. Reads relative offset, calculates target, and
--   delegates frame setup.
instCall :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements TAIL_CALL (Opcode 0x41).
--   
--   @details Optimized call. Replaces current frame (no snapshot pushed).
instTailCall :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements CALL_INDIRECT (Opcode 0x42).
--   
--   @details Pops the top value and delegates to
--   <a>dispatchIndirectCall</a>.
instCallIndirect :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements RET (Opcode 0x43).
--   
--   @details 1. Pops the return value from the top of the stack. 2.
--   Retrieves and removes the top <a>CallSnapshot</a>. 3. <a>Cleans</a>
--   the stack by truncating it to the start of the current frame. This
--   effectively discards all local variables. 4. Restores the Caller's
--   context (IP and FP). 5. Pushes the return value back onto the restored
--   stack.
--   
--   @throws Error "VM Error: Return called with empty call stack" if
--   executed in global scope.
instRet :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements MAKE_CLOSURE (Opcode 0x60).
--   
--   @details Reads arguments then checks if the stack has enough elements.
--   If yes, calls <a>pushClosure</a>.
instMakeClosure :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Implements GET_FUNC_ADDR (Opcode 0x61).
--   
--   @details Reads an absolute address (Int) and pushes it as a VFuncPtr.
--   Used to pass functions as values before potentially wrapping them in
--   closures.
instGetFuncAddr :: VirtualMachine ()


-- | This module orchestrates the execution of the Virtual Machine. It
--   fetches opcodes from the bytecode and dispatches them to the
--   appropriate instruction handlers defined in the Instruction modules.
module VM.Bytecode.Runner

-- | The main execution loop of the Virtual Machine.
--   
--   @details This function operates in a continuous cycle: 1. Checks if
--   the VM <a>isRunning</a> flag is True. 2. Fetches the next opcode using
--   <a>readByte</a>. 3. Calls <a>executeInstruction</a> to run the
--   associated logic. 4. Recursively calls itself to process the next
--   instruction.
--   
--   The loop terminates when <a>instHalt</a> sets <a>isRunning</a> to
--   False or if an error occurs (e.g., Stack Underflow).
runBytecode :: VirtualMachine ()

-- | Maps a raw opcode byte to its corresponding instruction function.
--   
--   @args - op: The 8-bit instruction code fetched from bytecode.
--   
--   @details This pattern matching acts as the specific <a>Decode</a> step
--   of the CPU cycle. Any unknown opcode will trigger a runtime error.
executeInstruction :: Word8 -> VirtualMachine ()
